sourceOfTruth.rule: Automatically generate and review client migration/snapshot and SQL files after the target build succeeds under the registered plan; no separate generation approval. The client DbContext, installed target model and generated output are authoritative. Database application is a separate explicitly approved deployment operation.

whenToRun: For every requested upgrade where a client DbContext exists, including patch/minor releases; inspect existing migrations and target-model impact rather than assuming no schema change from the version number.

contextDetection.selectionRule: Inspect the client's derived context, migrations assembly, startup project and design-time factory. Do not guess a context when multiple candidates exist; resolve from repository configuration or request the missing selection.
contextDetection.designTimeSafety: Verify context construction does not invoke Database.Migrate, EnsureCreated or another database write before running EF tooling.

review: Inspect existing output before generation; reuse a matching target migration on resume and never overwrite unrelated user migrations.
Review Up/Down, snapshot and SQL against the installed target model; inspect drops, truncation, lossy conversions, required-column backfills and foreign-key/data preconditions.
Retain a destructive draft as review evidence, not deployment-ready output; block affected acceptance/application pending explicit approval or resolution of data/business semantics.
Record database application and required prechecks in the deployment checklist; never run database update, execute SQL or start an auto-migrating host as generation validation.

retryRules.action: Search for the concrete DbContext and rerun with fully qualified --context.
Return to the build-fix loop before retrying migration.

retryRules.whenOutputContains: No migrations configuration type was found
retryRules.action: Retry with fully qualified context name.

antiPatterns: Do not run EF migration before build succeeds.
Do not manually edit the model snapshot without EF output evidence.
Do not treat no changes detected as failure.
Do not block generation/review just because a client migration is required.
Do not copy Core migration classes into the client's migration history blindly.
Do not repeatedly scaffold empty or duplicate migrations on resume.

successCriteria: Migration command exits successfully or reports no changes detected.
Generated migration, snapshot and SQL are reviewed and included in the final report when present; no-change or empty-migration outcomes are explicitly recorded.
Generated code rebuilds successfully. Destructive/data-semantic risks remain explicitly blocked until resolved or approved; database application is not performed.
